chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj on behalf of another person: Does that suffice for him for the Hajj of Islam (the obligatory Hajj)? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory Hajj (the first Hajn of Islam)

ai.seo_question: Does Hajj performed on behalf of someone else count as their obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that Hajj performed on behalf of another is valid for discharging the obligatory Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam), a ruling foundational to Shia jurisprudence regarding the transfer of religious duties. This establishes the permissibility of *Hajj al-Badal* for those unable to perform it themselves, distinguishing it from the voluntary Hajj which is not typically transferable. The confirmation by the Imam underscores the flexibility in fulfilling the pillar of Islam while maintaining its spiritual integrity.
